audit_findings.title: The $300 million receivables program may hide a material financing and working-capital dependency
audit_findings.magnitude: RPA principal increased from $300.0 million to $350.0 million, equal to $6.18 per diluted share and 11.9% of the $2.940 billion base equity value; purchaser fees were $15.767 million in FY2025 and $11.410 million for the first 39 weeks of FY2026
audit_findings.mechanism: Owner earnings are overstated if purchaser fees were removed or receivables-sale proceeds were treated as recurring operating cash; the equity bridge may also omit the cash requirement or financing consequences of rebuilding derecognized receivables when the program ends.
audit_findings.evidence: The total principal amount outstanding of receivables sold was approximately $ 300,000 as of August 30, 2025 and August 31, 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: No error is demonstrated. The latest 10-Q confirms that the RPA was renewed through December 8, 2028, expanded to $350.0 million, fully utilized, and that purchaser fees continued through other expense. The supplied record does not show the owner-earnings reconciliation needed to verify that those fees remained deducted or that receivables-sale cash flows were excluded. A hypothetical full $350.0 million adjustment would be meaningful to the stated value, although it would not close the large gap between the $57.84 bull value and the $121.41 market price. Operational or refinancing effects upon termination remain unquantified, so the record cannot establish overall materiality.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2023-FY2026 owner earnings to the RPA sale, collection and fee entries; confirm the $15.767 million FY2025 fees were deducted; then rerun scenarios for continued renewal and for a $350.0 million receivables rebuild or replacement financing at the December 2028 termination date.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved Macomb litigation could create a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Additional defense costs would reduce owner earnings, while damages, settlement payments or disgorgement attributable to the company would require an equity-bridge deduction or corresponding cash-flow adjustment.
audit_findings.evidence: At this time, the ultimate cost to resolve this matter is not reasonably estimable, however the Company believes it has substantial defenses to the alleged claims and intends to vigorously defend itself.
audit_findings.explanation: No valuation error or probable loss is demonstrated because the company has recorded no estimable liability and the filing provides no damages range. However, the motion to dismiss was denied on November 14, 2025 and an appeal was filed on February 20, 2026, so the exposure remains active rather than merely hypothetical. With unspecified damages, uncertain insurance or indemnification, and no allocation between the company and other defendants, the record cannot determine whether the claim is large enough to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain developments through September 5, 2026, the operative complaint's damages theory, appeal status, insurance limits and exclusions, indemnification obligations, company-versus-other-defendant allocation, legal-fee accruals and any settlement range; rerun owner earnings and the equity bridge once a company-funded amount is supportable.
